gay.guidance: “Gay” is a valid identity term for many people. Do not replace it with generic “people” or an umbrella label when referring to someone's orientation; follow the person's own wording and mention orientation only when relevant.

gays.guidance: Avoid using “gays” as a noun for people. If orientation is relevant, use “gay people” or the group's preferred wording; generic “people” can erase relevant identity.

bisexual.guidance: “Bisexual” is a valid identity term, not a synonym for all LGBTQIA+ people. Use it only when relevant and do not substitute generic “person.”

bisexuals.guidance: Avoid using “bisexuals” as a noun for people. If relevant, use “bisexual people”; do not replace the specific identity with an umbrella label or generic “people.”

lesbian.guidance: “Lesbian” is a valid identity term for many people. Use it only when relevant and follow the person's own wording; it is not interchangeable with every LGBTQIA+ identity or with “person.”

lesbians.guidance: Avoid using “lesbians” as a noun for people. If orientation is relevant, use “lesbian people” or the group's preferred wording.

homosexual.guidance: This can sound clinical or dated when used for a person. Prefer the person's own identity term when relevant; do not replace it with generic “people” by default.

homosexuals.guidance: This can sound clinical or dated when used for people. Avoid using it as a noun; use the group's own identity term when relevant rather than generic “people.”

same-sex.guidance: “Same-sex” describes a relationship or pairing, not an individual identity. A replacement such as “same-gender” is suitable only when that is what the context means.
